subject: Does munge function takes away too many SNPs?

messages.author: 02a680a9f46abb8a
messages.subject: Does munge function takes away too many SNPs?
parts:
Hi, is it normal to lose this many SNPs from the munge function?

[1] "Munging file: /genomic_sem/data1.gz"
[1] "Interpreting the RSID column as the SNP column."
[1] "Interpreting the A1 column as the A1 column."
[1] "Interpreting the A2 column as the A2 column."
[1] "Interpreting the OR column as the effect column."
[1] "Interpreting the P column as the P column."
[1] "Interpreting the N column as the N (sample size) column."
[1] "Interpreting the MAF column as the MAF (minor allele frequency) column."
[1] "Merging file: /genomic_sem/data1.gz with the reference file: /genomic_sem/w_hm3.snplist"
[1] "6904702 rows present in the full /genomic_sem/data1.gz summary statistics file."
[1] "6340291 rows were removed from the /genomic_sem/data1.gz summary statistics file as the rs-ids for these rows were not present in the reference file."
[1] "The effect column was determined to be coded as an odds ratio (OR) for the /genomic_sem/data1.gz summary statistics file. Please ensure this is correct."
[1] "No INFO column, cannot filter on INFO, which may influence results"
[1] "1145 rows were removed from the /genomic_sem/data1.gz summary statistics file due to missing MAF information or MAFs below the designated threshold of 0.001"
[1] "563370 SNPs are left in the summary statistics file /genomic_sem/data1.gz after QC."
[1] "I am done munging file: /genomic_sem/data1.gz"

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Does munge function takes away too many SNPs?
parts:
Hi there, 

Sorry for late response; It is normal to lose a large number of SNPs as it is merging with the HapMap3 file which only has 1.1 million SNPs to begin with. ~560,000 SNPs should be enough to produce interpretable results from LDSC and Genomic SEM. 

Best, 
  Andrew
